questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to entering traffic.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right and yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to your exit.

questions.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side. You cannot get completely through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do this even if you do not see other traffic. This is the law.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing where the crossing signals are flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Look for an oncoming train. Also watch for lowered crossing gates or listen for train sounds.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.
Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Watch for other drivers also moving into your lane. Do not use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions hurt your driving ability. Worry, anger, fear, and sadness reduce your focus. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Honk to alert drivers and pedestrians to your presence.
Increase your speed to avoid any pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. Someone may open a door and step out. A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center of your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is coming straight at you in your lane, honk your horn first to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because the other driver might swerve and hit you anyway. Brake hard and steadily. Slowing down even a little bit reduces the impact.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and are inflated to the correct pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go much faster or slower than other cars on the road. Always drive at the same speed as other traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge angles toward the middle. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
A construction area is ahead.
You must turn left soon.
The road gets narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road gets narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road's edge shows where the road ends. If the line angles toward the middle, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to rejoin the main road after a stop. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you see them.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to rejoin the main road after it has stopped to pick up or drop off passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you can't find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: You've done all you need to do.
Stay and wait for police.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit an unattended vehicle, try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and a description of the accident.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a warning and continue through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you that a traffic light is coming and you should prepare to stop or slow down.

questions.question: You see a sign that says '45 mph where workers present' in a work zone. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down right away.
Drive safely for the conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less if workers are there.
Move to the right lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely for the conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less if workers are there.
questions.explanation: In work zones with this sign, you must slow down to 45 mph or less when you see workers, but you can drive the normal speed limit when no workers are present. Always watch for workers and reduce speed when you see them.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: A recommended speed only.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The safest maximum speed under good road and weather conditions.
The safest maximum speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safest maximum speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the legal maximum speed for that road. Safe driving may require you to go slower than the posted limit. When conditions are bad, you should drive slower.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: It decreases the effects of both.
It increases the effects of both.
It helps cure your illness.
It improves your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. Driving is unsafe after drinking alcohol or taking drugs alone. It is much more dangerous when you combine them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look around, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: How do you pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to pass safely. Only pass if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal the driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay right when another driver passes on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: How should you treat railroad crossings?

options.text: They are safe because trains rarely come.
They are dangerous.
They are safe places to park.
You must always stop there.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic going in opposite directions. It means you can pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.
